summary: A production release focused on correctness, release-build parity, and the first bare-metal microcontroller targets.

highlights.title: Enumerate, map, and collect keep tuple values
highlights.text: Chained iterator calls now bind the mapping function's tuple return through collect, so indexed ranges keep both elements and field access reads the real payload.

highlights.title: Data-loss fixes for results and tuples
highlights.text: Direct error values pushed into vectors, vectors inside cross-module result tuples, and nested enum-variant matches now preserve their payloads.

highlights.title: Release builds match debug builds
highlights.text: A release-compiler parity job now runs the correctness probes from the optimized binary on Linux, Windows, and the ARM64 compiler floor.

highlights.title: Cortex-M and RISC-V microcontroller targets
highlights.text: New freestanding targets for Cortex-M and 32-bit RISC-V ship with a startup, linker, and runtime contract, plus emulator tests.

highlights.title: Lower memory use for confined loops
highlights.text: Copying a vector out of a confined block now only copies memory owned by the block, removing a large per-iteration leak in frame capture workloads.

highlights.title: Reusable receive buffers and guarded copy-out
highlights.text: socket_recv_into and socket_recv_timeout_into fill a caller-owned Vec and reuse its capacity, so per-connection read buffers stop allocating per request. The runtime also returns main-heap Vec buffers in place on confined-block exit, and JSON number rendering is allocation-free.

known_issues: Microcontroller targets use a bump allocator and do not support exceptions; vendor peripherals are not emulated.
